findings.issue: Incorrectly resolved F-06: G4.6 runs `jj -R $U new main` BEFORE G4.7 runs the §7 fitness gate and moves `main` to the G4 tip. At step 6, `main` is still at the G3 tip, so `jj -R $U new main` replaces `$U`'s working tree on disk with G3 `main` (wiping the 998 `W` files from `$U` before G4 passes §7 or lands in `main`). Additionally, G4.4 moves binaries and edits `.gitignore` before G4.6 runs `jj -R $U status`; mutating `$U` before G4.6 causes `jj -R $U status` to snapshot those changes into `suukkrkqkwuv`, creating a new divergent commit on `suukkrkqkwuv`.
findings.recommendation: Do not modify `$U` during G4.1–G4.5 (edit `.gitignore` in the G4 merge workspace, not in `$U`). Execute G4.7 (`§7` fitness gate -> lease -> `jj bookmark set main` to G4 tip) BEFORE G4.6, and only after `main` has advanced to the G4 tip run `jj -R $U new main` and move any remaining untracked/ignored binaries from `$U` to `$BK/binaries/`.

findings.issue: Partially unresolved F-07 and Gap 1: §9 (line 500) still uses the placeholder `<coordinator-lib>/*/ebin` while §2.2 (line 91) states that both known `session_sync_cli` builds refuse replay (`journal sequence or digest mismatch`), and G0.2 provides no concrete query or workspace path to locate the adapter Codex used for events 1977–1979. Additionally, Header line 17 and §16.1 ('Preconditions (before G0.4)') leave ambiguous whether `G0_PRESERVE` must be claimed in Sa-plan (§8) before G0.1 begins, as required by R2 ('work without a ledger triggers an Andon stop').
findings.recommendation: In G0.2, specify the exact discovery steps (e.g., `sqlite3 -readonly var/coordination/tri-agent/coordinator.sqlite3 'SELECT * FROM events WHERE seq >= 1977;'` and checking `.uos-workspaces/codex-telegram-mainline-20261025` / `codex-coordinator-recovery-20261024` for the working `session_sync_cli` ebin) and replace `<coordinator-lib>` in §9. Explicitly require claiming `G0_PRESERVE` in Sa-plan (with `--preflight` and `--active-check`) before G0.1.

findings.issue: G0.7 extracts only `$BK/jj.tar` into `$BK/restore` and runs `jj -R $BK/restore log ...`, claiming '`jj -R` on a `.jj` copy with no working copy is read-only; if jj insists on a working copy, restore both tars into one scratch tree'. In `jj 0.44`, `$BK/restore` is the working copy root for `$BK/restore/.jj`; running `jj -R $BK/restore` without `--ignore-working-copy` does not error out—instead, `jj` automatically snapshots the empty `$BK/restore` directory as a mass deletion of all tracked files in `@` (`suukkrkqkwuv`), mutating the restored repository state. Furthermore, because `jj` never 'insists on a working copy', `$BK/default-wc.tar` (the 998 `W` files) is never restore-tested locally or on `vm-1`.
findings.recommendation: In G0.7 and G0.8(b), unconditionally extract both `$BK/jj.tar` and `$BK/default-wc.tar` into `$BK/restore` before running verification commands, pass `--ignore-working-copy` on read-only `jj -R $BK/restore` inspection commands, and verify `jj -R $BK/restore status` matches live `$U`.

findings.issue: In G2.8, G3.5, G4.7, G5.4, and G6, the step order is `§7 -> move -> journal`, which contradicts §7's `Docs` row (`tools/journal-check <journal>` must pass before `main` moves) and causes every generation journal to be committed after `jj bookmark set main`, stranding it outside `::main`. Furthermore, in G0, G1, and G7, §5.4 specifies '`main` after: unchanged', and §6 line 355 / G2.1 write journals and `merge-g2-ledger.json` 'in the executor's workspace' rather than `$M`. Consequently, none of the G0–G7 journals, the G1.1 lineage note, or the G2.1 ledger ever become ancestors of `main`.
findings.recommendation: Write and commit each generation's journal and ledger into `$M`'s candidate commit BEFORE running the §7 `Docs` row (`journal-check`, `diagram-check`, `timestamp-check`) and BEFORE moving `main` (`journal -> §7 -> lease and move`). Include the G0/G1 journals, G1.1 lineage note, and G2.1 ledger in the G2 candidate commit in `$M`, and advance `main` under lease in G7.4 for the final programme journal.

findings.issue: G2.7 and the §7 Telegram row (for G2–G6) instruct Codex to re-run the 25 HTTP/browser groups using 'scripts under `var/recovery-runtime/20261025-0559-mini-chat-flow5/`'. That directory is a frozen runtime snapshot from 05:59Z, whereas the repo-tracked build and fixture scripts (`tools/validation/build_recovery_fixtures.sh`, `tools/validation/telegram_mini_candidate/build.js`, `prepare-fixture.js`, `restoration_browser_check.ml`) are among the 113 deferred files landing in `$M` during G2. Running the `05:59Z` recovery-runtime scripts directly tests stale binaries rather than `$M`'s generation tip, violating §4.3 rule 1 and R7.
findings.recommendation: Require G2.7 (and §7 for G2–G6) to build a fresh recovery-runtime fixture from `$M` at the candidate tip using `$M/tools/validation/build_recovery_fixtures.sh` and `$M/tools/validation/telegram_mini_candidate/build.js` before executing the 25 HTTP/browser groups against that build.

findings.issue: G1.5 runs the full §7 matrix on `main` (`2ab40165`) even though `2ab40165` omits 47 `A` files and differs on 66 `M` files across `apps/cepaf_gleam`, `engines/hermes`, `formal/lean`, `plugins/uos-risk-prioritization/validation` (including `A reclaim_metadata.ml`, `A reviewed_selection.ml`, `M dune`), and `tools/uos`. Line 387 states that if G1.5 fails, Codex should either roll `main` back to `a8adcc69` (§4.3 rule 6) or open a P1 repair task on top of `main`. Rolling `main` back to `a8adcc69` invalidates G1.6 and G2 (whose 113-file list is diffed against `2ab40165`, leaving no generation to re-merge the 198 files of `A'`), while a repair commit on `main` contradicts §5.4 (`G1 main after: unchanged`) unless the 113-file diff is recomputed.
findings.recommendation: In G1.5, separate (a) failures in `engines/hermes`, `plugins/uos-risk-prioritization/validation`, `formal/lean`, or `tools/uos` caused by files deferred to G2 (which should be resolved by integrating those files in G2) from (b) regressions inside `A'`/`M1` itself (which should be fixed via a leased commit on `main` in G1 followed by regenerating the G2 diff list against the new `main`). Forbid rolling `main` back to `a8adcc69` without triggering a §16.2 replanning stop.

findings.issue: G6 instructs B1's owner (Codex, in `codex-agy-ops-20261024`) and B2's owner (AGY, in `agy-telemetry-20261024`) to run `jj rebase -s <first own commit> -d main` in their own workspaces, followed immediately by `§7 -> move -> journal`. (1) Rebasing B1 and B2 onto `main` in two separate owner workspaces produces two sibling heads outside `$M`; G6 specifies no command in `$M` to combine or sequentially integrate the rebased `B1'` and `B2'` after their uncurated trunk ancestry has been stripped. (2) AGY runs as a bounded Sa-plan job rather than a persistent workspace daemon, so G6 lacks a dispatch step to invoke AGY for B2.
findings.recommendation: Specify in G6 that (1) Codex dispatches a bounded Sa-plan job for AGY to rebase B2 in `agy-telemetry-20261024` (or leaves B2 in `preserved/*` if unavailable), and (2) once `B1'` (and `B2'`) are rebased onto `main` and verified free of `::preserved/trunk-a2-20261025 ~ ::main` ancestry, Codex merges the rebased commits in `$M` (`jj -R $M new main <B1'> -m ...` / `jj -R $M new @ <B2'> -m ...`), runs §7 in `$M`, and then moves `main`.

findings.issue: Partially unresolved Gap 4: G0.8(a) instructs Codex to run `jj git push --remote origin --dry-run -b main -b 'glob:preserved/*' -b 'glob:recovery/*'` and then repeat without `--dry-run`. Because `preserved/snapshot-x1` (`4452207cf7f6`) and `preserved/snapshot-x2` (`0e75c0ffe417`) have `(none)` (empty) commit descriptions (§3 lines 142–143) and R4 forbids describing commits authored by others, `jj git push` in `jj 0.44` will refuse the push unless `--allow-empty-description` is passed or empty-description commits are excluded from the push set.
findings.recommendation: Exclude `preserved/snapshot-x1` and `preserved/snapshot-x2` from the `origin` push set (per N-01), and if any remaining `preserved/*` commit has an empty description, pass `--allow-empty-description` to `jj git push` in G0.8(a).

findings.issue: G1.3 runs `cp $U/apps/cepaf_gleam/priv/*.so $U/apps/cepaf_gleam/priv/*.sha256 $M/apps/cepaf_gleam/priv/` and then checks `apps/cepaf_gleam/priv/*.sha256 | sha256sum -c -` from `$M`. Copying both `*.so` and `*.sha256` from dirty `$U` (`default`, which has 998 uncommitted `W` files) only checks that `$U`'s files match themselves and overwrites any repo-tracked `.sha256` files in `$M` (dirtying `@`). Additionally, G1.4 creates a 'second provisioned workspace at `recovery/pre-merge-20261025`' without specifying a workspace name/path or forgetting it in G7.1.
findings.recommendation: In G1.3, copy only untracked `*.so` binaries into `$M` and verify them against `$M`'s tracked `.sha256` files (or verify `jj -R $M status` is clean after provisioning). In G1.4, specify `jj workspace add --name baseline-20261025 -r recovery/pre-merge-20261025 $U/.uos-workspaces/baseline-20261025` and `jj workspace forget baseline-20261025` once baseline counts are recorded.

findings.issue: §5.1 Rule 1 mandates 'P1 (loss and evidence integrity) first, then P2, then P3.' In §5.2, `D-ev September evidence` (10 heads D1..D10) is classified as Class P3 with score 24 and medium merge risk, yet it is bundled into G5 ahead of Class P2 units `B1/B2 grafts` (P2, score 48, G6) and `Workspace/bookmark/unit prune` (P2, score 108, G7) without an override in §5.3, and §8 registers `G5_ARCHIVE` with priority 108 (`D-code`).
findings.recommendation: Either split Class P3 `D-ev September evidence` (score 24) into a post-G6/G7 P3 generation (keeping only P2 `D-code EV-01 fixes`, score 108, in G5), or document an explicit archive-cohesion override in §5.3 with a rule that any failing `D-ev` head is immediately seed-banked without delaying G6 or G7.

findings.issue: G7.1 scans candidate workspaces for untracked files using `find <ws> -type f -newer <ws>/.jj -not -path '*/build/*' -not -path '*/_build/*'`. Running `jj -R <ws> status` immediately beforehand updates working-copy state inside `<ws>/.jj/`, so any untracked or gitignored artifact older than `<ws>/.jj` fails `-newer <ws>/.jj` and is omitted from `$BK/workspaces/<ws>.tar`, while omitting `-not -path '*/.jj/*'` includes `.jj` internal files in the scan.
findings.recommendation: Replace `-newer <ws>/.jj` in G7.1 with `-not -path '*/.jj/*' -not -path '*/target/*'` (comparing `find` results against `jj -R <ws> file list --ignore-working-copy`) so all non-build untracked and gitignored artifacts are archived regardless of `.jj` timestamps.

Verifies exact `jj 0.44` push flags, `.sha256` trailing-provenance `awk` parsing, comma-separated Sa-plan dependency syntax, and nanosecond vs second lease units.
